CHAPTER VI
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 17
(1) The City Regional Government implements prevention efforts against the occurrence of violence toward Women and Children in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;

c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection of Child Victims of Violence.

a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

CHAPTER VI
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 17
(1) The City Regional Government implements prevention efforts against the occurrence of violence toward Women and Children in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) The City Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence against Children

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City Region is the City Region of Banjar.
2. City Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Banjar.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government that is the authority of the region.
6. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
7. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
9. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs within the Regional territory.
11. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
12. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
13. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
14. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their roles normally again both in the family and in society.
15. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
16. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise.
17. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
18. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will, is and/or has occurred.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical support activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
22. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

Article 7
Letter a What is meant by "network" is the working partner of the Regional Government in the implementation of prevention of violence against women in the form of family partners, among others family groups, and dasawisma.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c What is meant by "socialization" is the dissemination of information on laws and regulations carried out through mass media, electronic media, and/or direct counseling to the community.

Article 12
(1) Prevention of Violence against Children as referred to in Article 11 letter a shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to Prevent Violence against Children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Violence Prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) Prevention of Violence against Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 22
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by "medical services" is a form of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the field of law.
Letter b What is meant by "medicolegal services" is treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
Letter c What is meant by "psychosocial services" is services provided by companions in the context of traumatic recovery of the victim's condition including the provision of space and safe houses to protect victims from threats and intimidation.
Letter d What is meant by "legal services" is services to victims in undergoing legal processes.
Letter e What is meant by "social reintegration" is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family/institutions, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
Letter f What is meant by "economic independence services" is services for skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.

4.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Article 17(1) explicitly states prevention efforts include “melakukan pendidikan tentang nilai anti kekerasan terhadap Perempuan dan Anak” (conducting education on anti-violence values toward women and children). This is clearly prevention through education. The retrieved English passage accurately reflects this, and the judge’s reasoning matches the Indonesian ground truth. Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

6.3.rationale: The Indonesian text mentions work/employment only in the context of empowering women victims of violence (Pasal 10(1): “pelatihan kerja”; and in the explanation of Pasal 10(2) huruf a: women victims “berhak untuk bekerja dan berusaha…”). This is not a targeted intersectional provision about “women workers” as a distinct group (e.g., protections tailored to female workers, workplace violence/harassment, labor-sector measures). The retrieved passages contained the same limited content; the error is the judge’s lenient mapping from generic ‘right to work’ to ‘women workers’.

This is a general non-discrimination clause and does not explicitly mention disability (“disabilitas”, “penyandang disabilitas”) or provide disability-specific accommodations/accessibility measures. The judge treated “physical or mental condition” as implicitly covering disability and answered Yes, but the golden label indicates the indicator requires explicit disability mention or specific provisions. Since the relevant text was available and correctly translated, the discrepancy is best explained by the judge’s overly broad interpretation.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian explanation of Pasal 3 huruf b lists non-discrimination grounds (suku, agama, ras, golongan, jenis kelamin, etnis, budaya dan bahasa, status hukum, kondisi fisik/mental). While this is a broad equality statement, it does not explicitly identify or address “minority groups” as a targeted intersectional group with tailored measures; it is framed as general non-discrimination in service delivery. The judge equated a general non-discrimination list with an affirmative mention/approach to minority groups and answered Yes. Because the relevant passage was retrieved and the issue is interpretive leniency rather than missing evidence, this is an evaluation failure.
